content:
Why NGO moves need extra planning

Nonprofits and NGOs in Addis Ababa often sit near Old Airport, Kazanchis, and Bole diplomatic corridors. You are moving more than desks—grant files, donor correspondence, and IT with donor reporting deadlines need chain-of-custody and quiet weekend windows when neighbors include embassies and residential towers.

Two weeks before

  • Inventory filing cabinets and sealed donor records; decide what may move in locked bins vs digital-only.
  • Coordinate IT cutover with your vendor—movers handle physical gear, not database migration.
  • Confirm building freight rules at origin and destination; some towers limit weekend noise.
  • Submit crew ID lists and truck plates where security requires 48-hour notice.
  • Brief volunteers on what not to pack (original signed agreements stay with legal lead).

Move weekend structure

Many NGOs move Friday evening through Sunday: labeled workstations, sealed record bins with sign-off sheets, and IT reconnect before Monday staff return. Phased moves split programs across two weekends if seat count exceeds one freight block.

Security-sensitive sites

Embassy-adjacent offices may need manifests earlier than residential condos. Share supervisor contact with both buildings’ security desks—delays at the gate burn hourly quotes if scope is open-ended; prefer fixed commercial quotes—hourly vs fixed.

Volunteer coordination

Volunteers should not ad-hoc pack donor originals—legal lead assigns sealed bins. Movers follow the floor plan, not improvised hallway sorting.

Reliability

Donors expect professionalism—reliable mover checklist before you sign.

Grant audit trail

Keep mover invoices and gate permits with grant files if donors require relocation documentation. Itemized commercial quotes beat cash receipts from brokers—delala vs professional.

Hybrid staff schedules

Some NGOs split teams: half move Friday, half Monday, to keep a skeleton desk for donor calls. Movers phase cartons by department color to match that plan.

Fixed commercial quote

Request itemized office scope—hourly vs fixed—so gate delays in Kirkos do not inflate an open meter. Plate confirmation before load is standard Active Movers dispatch practice.
